description:
​I am participating as a solo innovator for NASA Space Apps Kuala Lumpur 2026.
​My chosen challenge is "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer". I am focusing on designing an interactive UI/UX prototype and presentation using Canva for this challenge.
summary: NB Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a free, browser-based training game for children aged 8 to 12. It turns astronaut preparation into three short stations. In the first, kids see how their weight changes on the Moon, Mars, Earth and Jupiter using real gravity values. In the second, they pack a 10 kg crew bag and learn that oxygen, water, food and a medkit come before fun items. In the third, a five-question quiz covers the International Space Station, spacewalk training and the Artemis program, with a short explanation after every answer. Finishing all three stations earns a crew badge and a rank. The trainer answers the challenge by making real astronaut training ideas simple and fun to practise. It matters because early, playful contact with space science can inspire the next generation of explorers. It needs no install or login and works on phones and computers.
details:
NB Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a free, browser-based training game for children aged 8 to 12. It has three stations and a crew badge.

How it works: Station 1 uses real gravity values to show a child's weight on the Moon, Mars, Earth and Jupiter. Station 2 asks the child to pack a 10 kg crew bag. Oxygen, water, food and a medkit are required, and extra items such as a giant teddy bear make the bag too heavy, which teaches mission trade-offs. Station 3 is a five-question quiz on the International Space Station, spacewalk training, the Artemis program and Moon gravity, with a short explanation after every answer. Finishing all three stations earns a Crew Badge and a rank based on the quiz score.

Benefits and impact: It turns astronaut preparation into play, supports classroom and home learning, and needs no login, install or data collection.

Tools: HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript in a single file, designed for phones, computers, light and dark mode and keyboard use. The demo deck was built with Claude.

Creativity: the packing task makes children feel real mission limits, and every answer explains why.

Factors considered: simple language, no ads, no NASA logos or branding, and accessibility.

Next steps: more missions (Moon base, Mars), more languages including Bahasa Malaysia and Bangla, and a teacher mode.
